title: Say it once, then keep walking straight.
subtitle: Faith that is said and then stood on
then: The verse comes right after the warning to wrongdoers and good news to the doers of good. It describes those who say {idea}our Lord is Allah{/idea} and then stay on that course. Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}no fear about what is ahead, no grief over what they left behind.{/reward}
now: You felt it strongly in Ramadan. The prayers were on time, the phone was down. Then the ordinary weeks came back. {idea}This verse praises the staying, not just the starting.{/idea} Small and steady still counts as standing firm.
old: My faith only counts when I feel it strongly.
new: What counts is saying it and then quietly staying on the path day after day.
try: Choose one small act of worship you can keep every day this week, and start today.

title: A home that lasts, for what they kept doing.
subtitle: Paradise as the reward of a steady life
then: Those who said our Lord is Allah and stood firm are called {reward}the companions of Paradise, forever.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes the phrase for what they used to do: {idea}their deeds are a cause for reaching mercy and being surrounded by it.{/idea}
now: You keep a habit you cannot see paying off: a monthly charity transfer, a call to your mother every Sunday. It feels small. {idea}The verse says used to do: the repeated things.{/idea} {reward}Mercy meets what you kept doing.{/reward}
old: My small, repeated good deeds do not really add up to anything.
new: What I keep doing becomes a door for Allah's mercy.
try: Pick one good thing you already do regularly and do it today with intention.

title: Thirty months of her hardship, and a prayer at forty.
subtitle: Gratitude to parents and turning back at maturity
then: Right after speaking of faith, the verse turns to parents, as the Quran often does. Ibn Kathir describes {trap}the fatigue, sickness, heaviness and pain{/trap} a mother bears, and the thirty months of carrying and nursing. At forty, a person's mind and patience mature. {idea}Ibn Kathir says this is a call for anyone reaching forty to renew repentance.{/idea}
now: Your mother's text says she has not heard from you in a while. You are busy, a deadline, a meeting. Thirty months of your life she carried and fed you before you could say thanks. {reward}The prayer here thanks Allah for her too.{/reward} And it asks good for your own children.
old: My parents did what parents do. I will thank them when life slows down.
new: My parents' hardship is a gift I owe thanks for, to them and to Allah, now.
try: Call or message one of your parents today just to thank them for one specific thing.

title: Their best is accepted, their worst is overlooked.
subtitle: The promise for those who turn back

picture.label: What Allah does with their record

then: This is for the person in the verse before: grateful, praying for parents and children, turning back to Allah. Ibn Kathir says {reward}many of their errors will be forgiven and a modest amount of deeds will be accepted.{/reward} {idea}It is a promise of truth.{/idea}
now: You replay your worst moments at 2am: the shouting, the lie, the wasted years. You feel your good is too small to matter. {reward}This verse describes a Lord who takes the best and overlooks the rest{/reward} for those who turn back.
old: My mistakes outweigh anything good I have done.
new: When I turn back, Allah keeps my best and overlooks my worst.
try: Say one sincere sentence of repentance tonight, then name one good thing you did today.

title: Uff to his parents, while they pray for him.
subtitle: The other kind of child, and his parents' pleading
then: After the grateful child comes the opposite. Ibn Kathir says this is a general description of anyone who speaks to parents with contempt and denies resurrection. He notes the claim it was about Abdur-Rahman bin Abi Bakr is weak, and Aishah rejected it. {reward}The parents keep asking Allah to guide him.{/reward}
now: Your mother reminds you to pray and you roll your eyes, sigh, say not now. {trap}Uff is that sigh.{/trap} {reward}Meanwhile she is making dua for you every night.{/reward} Even when you disagree, the tone is the deed.
old: A sigh or an eye roll at my parents is not a big deal.
new: My tone to my parents matters, and their worried prayers for me deserve gentleness.
try: The next time a parent nags you today, answer with one soft sentence instead of a sigh.

title: Joining the line of those who lost before.
subtitle: Where that attitude ends up
then: Ibn Kathir says the word those confirms the previous verse describes a type of person, not one man. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said it is {trap}the disbelieving, sinful one who is undutiful to his parents and denies resurrection.{/trap} Such people end up with their likes from earlier generations.
now: It is easy to read this and think of someone else's rude son. {idea}The verse describes a pattern, so it is a mirror.{/idea} Contempt at home and dismissing the Hereafter tend to travel together. {reward}The pattern can be broken today.{/reward}
old: This is about some bad person from long ago.
new: This describes a pattern, and I can check myself for any piece of it.
try: Ask yourself honestly how you spoke to your parents this week. Fix one thing.

title: Everyone gets their exact level, and no one is wronged.
subtitle: Degrees for both sides, perfect fairness
then: After the grateful child and the scornful one, the verse says all have degrees. Ibn Kathir quotes Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd: {idea}the levels of the Fire descend, and those of Paradise ascend.{/idea} {reward}Allah will not wrong anyone, even by a speck of dust.{/reward}
now: At work, the person who does the least gets the same bonus as you. It stings. {idea}Here nothing is averaged out.{/idea} {reward}Every kind word to your parents, every hidden effort, gets its exact weight.{/reward}
old: What I do does not really change much in the end.
new: Every deed shifts my level, and none of it is lost or unfairly counted.
try: Do one good thing today that nobody will see, knowing it is counted exactly.

title: You spent all your good things in the world.
subtitle: Pleasure used up, arrogance answered
then: On the Day the disbelievers face the Fire, they are told they used up their good things in this life. Ibn Kathir says Umar bin Al-Khattab {idea}gave up many joys of food and drink, afraid of being like those reproached here.{/idea} {trap}Their arrogance and rebellion are answered with humiliation.{/trap}
now: Payday comes and the cart fills fast: food delivery, a new gadget, the upgrade. {idea}None of it is wrong in itself.{/idea} But if every good thing is spent on the now, with no thanks and no giving, {trap}the verse says something is being used up.{/trap}
old: I worked for it, so I should enjoy all of it right now.
new: Blessings are for thanks and sharing, not only for using up.
try: Skip one small treat today and give its price to someone in need.

title: Remember the brother of Aad, warning his own people.
subtitle: Hud among the sand dunes
then: Ibn Kathir says this story was told {reward}to console the Prophet ﷺ{/reward} as his people rejected him. Hud was sent to Aad at al-Ahqaf, a land of sand dunes; Qatadah said in Yemen. The surah takes its name from here. {idea}Other warners had come before and after him.{/idea}
now: You are the only one in the family who prays, or who speaks up at work about something wrong. It feels lonely. {reward}The verse says: remember those who stood where you stand.{/reward} Hud was a brother to his people, not a stranger shouting at them.
old: Nobody has ever been as alone as I am in this.
new: Others stood in the same spot before me, and their stories are told to steady me.
try: Read one short story of a Prophet today and notice what he faced.

title: Bring it on, if you are telling the truth.
subtitle: Daring the warning to come

row.title: bring it
sub: the threat, if it is real

then: Aad accused Hud of trying to pull them from their gods. Then they said {trap}bring us what you threaten us with.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains they asked to hurry the punishment because they believed it would not happen.
now: The doctor says cut down on sugar or there will be trouble. You laugh and order dessert: show me. {trap}Daring a warning feels brave in the moment.{/trap} {idea}It usually just means you do not believe it yet.{/idea}
old: If it were really coming, it would have happened already.
new: Daring a warning is not courage; it is not believing it.
try: Think of one warning you have been laughing off. Take one small step toward it today.

title: When it comes is with Allah; my job is to tell you.
subtitle: Hud knows his role and its limits
then: Hud did not take the bait. Ibn Kathir paraphrases: {idea}Allah knows best about you; my duty is to deliver my message.{/idea} {trap}He told them plainly they were a people with no understanding.{/trap}
now: You advised your brother about a bad deal. He says, so when will it fail then? You cannot answer that. {idea}You can only say what you believe is true, kindly, and leave the outcome.{/idea}
old: If I give advice, I have to be able to prove exactly how it plays out.
new: My part is to say the truth clearly; the timing and results belong to Allah.
try: Give one honest piece of advice today and let go of needing to win the argument.

title: They saw a cloud and thought it was rain.
subtitle: What they cheered was what they had asked for

key.label: The habit of the Prophet ﷺ

then: Aad were in a drought, so a dark cloud made them glad. {trap}It was the wind they had asked to hurry.{/trap} Aishah said that when the Prophet ﷺ saw clouds or wind, worry showed on his face. {idea}He asked Allah for its good and sought refuge from its harm, and was relieved when rain fell.{/idea}
now: A big offer lands in your inbox. Everyone says it is perfect. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ would greet even welcome things with a prayer.{/idea} Not fear, just humility: you cannot always see what a cloud carries.
old: Anything that looks good coming my way must be good.
new: I can welcome what comes with a prayer for its good and protection from its harm.
try: Next time it rains or the wind picks up, ask Allah for its good and refuge from its harm.
